Rein 1.0.1

  • Quit Rein, and your Mac is stock again, charging included. Until now a charge limit kept holding after you quit Rein, while fans, sleep and display changes were handed back. Now quitting hands back all of it: the charge limit is released the moment Rein quits, and also if Rein ever crashes. Open Rein again and your limit is back. If you updated from 1.0, quitting works straight away; the crash case starts working after your next restart, when the background helper updates.
  • The charge limit works on macOS 27 again. macOS 27 (and the 26.7 and 15.8 updates) no longer lets apps pause charging. On those Macs Rein now sets Apple's own Charge Limit for you (80–100%), which macOS holds itself, awake or asleep, and shows in System Settings › Battery. A limit below 80% is held by switching wall power instead: the Mac runs from its battery from the limit down to the bottom of the sailing band, then charges back up, while it is awake. The Battery page says which method your Mac is using. Quitting Rein or pressing Reset to Auto puts Apple's limit back the way you had it. If Optimized Battery Charging is on, macOS may still hold at 80% on its own.
  • Battery health on macOS 27. Capacity and health read correctly again (macOS moved the figures), and the temperature comes from the Mac's own sensor.
  • Menu-bar tidy on macOS 27. macOS 27 draws the menu bar differently, and hiding icons stopped working there. Rein's divider now uses macOS 27's own overflow to hide the icons left of it, and clicking macOS's « shows them in their usual places (macOS's own peek would draw them over the app's menus); a click on the divider, or the 15-second timer, tucks them away again. Tucking back icons that other apps move is not yet possible on 27.
  • No more repeated password prompts from the remote. On some Macs, using the phone remote could make macOS ask for the login keychain password many times in a row. Rein now reads each saved item once, so it can ask at most once.

Rein 1.0

  • Rein is 1.0. Thank you to everyone who ran the 0.x releases.
  • The free trial is now 7 days from your first launch, with every feature and no card. If you installed Rein in the last week, your trial now runs to day 7.
  • Licence codes arrive in a minute. Buy on Ko-fi and collect your code straight away on the claim page with the email you paid with; Ko-fi's after-payment message has the link.
  • A one-time activation report. When you unlock Rein with a code, it tells our licence service once that the code is in use on this Mac: the code, an anonymous identifier for the Mac (a one-way scramble of its hardware ID) and the app version. Your licence is still checked on your Mac, keeps working offline, and this report can never lock you out. Details in the privacy policy at undercoverzest.app/rein.

Rein 0.9.10

  • Email-code gate: Check just works. Rein now reads everything it needs from the page's own sign-in redirect — no Cloudflare API, nothing to paste. The setup sheet shows one clear status line; the Cloudflare steps fold away until you need them.
  • Your iPhone stays trusted after a browser session. Allowing a second device (a laptop browser) no longer replaces the phone's saved pairing — every device you've allowed stays allowed.
  • Rein Remote can show you the browser address. The Mac now publishes the web remote's address to the phone; Rein Remote 0.2.5 shows it (with the Mac's name and the pairing code) in the Controls drawer.
  • Web remote fills the window instead of showing the Mac's screen small in a corner.
